harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 via /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app: daily, rotate 7, compress + delaycompress (7 compressed rotations retained), copytruncate so the app keeps writing to the same inode without needing a restart/signal. Verified with a dry-run and two forced live rotations that files rotate, compress on the following cycle, and that writes appended immediately after rotation land correctly. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the logrotate config, app.log data, and logrotate.timer all survived and remained healthy post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL 9.8, logrotate 3.18.0-12, /var/log/inventory/app.log present, logrotate.timer enabled/active, no pre-existing config for this log)
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Validated config syntax with logrotate -d
Forced a live rotation (logrotate -f -v); confirmed copytruncate truncated app.log to 0 bytes while preserving content in app.log.1
Appended new content to app.log post-rotation to prove the app can keep writing without interruption
Forced a second rotation; confirmed delaycompress produced app.log.2.gz (previous rotation compressed) while the newest rotation (app.log.1) stayed uncompressed as expected
Cleaned up test rotation artifacts and restored app.log to its original baseline content; reset logrotate.status
Captured baseline boot_id and service health on node1
Triggered systemctl reboot via a backgrounded/delayed shell so the exec ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed boot_id changed (98aa35f5... -> f168820a...) and new uptime start time, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart recovery: logrotate config file persisted, logrotate.timer active/enabled, app.log data intact, logrotate -d still recognizes the rule

evidence.requirement: Baseline state before rotation config (log file, logrotate binary, no prior config)
evidence.summary: Confirmed app.log exists, logrotate installed, logrotate.timer enabled/active, and no pre-existing logrotate rule for inventory app.

evidence.requirement: Logrotate config created (daily, rotate 7, compression, copytruncate)
evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with the required daily/rotate 7/compress/delaycompress/copytruncate settings and displayed the installed file.
logrotate -d dry run parsed the config without errors and correctly evaluated the rotation schedule.

evidence.requirement: Rotation actually occurs and retains compressed history (7 rotations) while app keeps writing after rotation (copytruncate)
evidence.summary: First forced rotation: copytruncate truncated app.log to 0 bytes and preserved prior content in app.log.1. After truncation, new content was appended to app.log and a second forced rotation moved it to app.log.1 while the earlier app.log.1 was compressed to app.log.2.gz per delaycompress, proving both the rotate/retain/compress pipeline and uninterrupted app writes post-rotation.

evidence.requirement: Cleanup / final steady state of app.log and config
evidence.summary: Removed test rotation artifacts, restored app.log to original baseline content, and reconfirmed the logrotate config file remains in place.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart protocol: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (98aa35f5-6905-42fd-9f07-0e28f75b4fa6), uptime start, and logrotate.timer active/enabled status prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart protocol: restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued systemctl reboot via a backgrounded delayed shell; the exec call returned 'reboot scheduled' successfully before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart protocol: node unreachable during reboot, then changed boot identity confirmed
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection timeouts/resets while node1 was rebooting, then a successful exec returned a new boot_id (f168820a-9f12-4e23-a26f-d37f5cc6f1a1) and new uptime start (08:21:46), proving an actual restart rather than mere service recovery.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart protocol: post-restart recovery of required services/config/data
evidence.summary: After reboot, confirmed /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app persisted intact, app.log data intact, logrotate.timer active and enabled, and logrotate -d still validates the rule correctly.
